content:
Alex: Quick sync — I pushed the initial PRD for the request-orchestration policy (v0.1). Need eyes on: tier definitions, cross-region failover, and what we call 'compatible variants'. Link: https://redwood.internal/prd/request-orchestration
Maya: skimmed it. main Q — how strict is 'compatible'? tokenizer differences make some fallbacks unsafe. do we allow a tokenizer shim or block fallback?
Sam: +1 tokenizer is the big one. if tokenization differs we can get garbage outputs. either require same tokenizer or add a cheap translation step (risky).
Priya: Suggest measurable acceptance criteria: for auto-fallback, run 1k canonical prompts and require embedding cosine >= 0.90 AND top-k ngram similarity >= 0.75. if either fails, block auto-fallback and only allow manual opt-in.
Jon: Edge-case: KV cache continuity between variants. if fallback model has different KV layout or layer dims we must flush cache or risk hallucinations. add explicit invalidation policy per-variant.
Casey: Launch checklist idea — must have: docs for ops, canary in two regions, perf guardrails (P99 < baseline * 1.05), cost guardrails that cap extra spend, and a rollback runbook wired into Console.
Alex: Agree on checklist. Proposal: tiers = [latency-sensitive, throughput-batch, best-effort]. Latency-sensitive: prefer low-latency model family, no quantized fallback unless compatibility score >= 0.95. Throughput-batch: allow quantized fallback down to 4-bit if quality tests pass. Best-effort: aggressive fallbacks allowed.
Maya: here's a tiny config sketch for the policy (non-normative):
```json
{
  "tiers": {
    "low_latency": { "preferred": ["rw-llama-70b"], "fallbacks": ["rw-llama-70b-q4"], "compat_threshold": 0.95 },
    "throughput": { "preferred": ["rw-llama-70b-q4"], "fallbacks": ["rw-mistral-8k-q4"], "compat_threshold": 0.85 }
  },
  "regions": ["us-west-2","eu-west-1"],
  "failover_order": ["same-region","peer-region","global-capacity"],
  "compat_checks": ["tokenizer_align","embed_cosine","ngram_overlap"]
}
```
Sam: That looks reasonable. we should also encode a fallback TTL for cached prefixes: e.g., if fallback happens, invalidate cached KV for that session to avoid token mismatch.
Priya: Acceptance criteria concrete wording for PRD: (1) automated compatibility test completes in <= 10m per model; (2) fallback causes no more than 2% decrease in semantic eval score on the defined corpus; (3) rollout can be automatically rolled back within 5m via console.
Jon: Add an edge case for multi-tenant private deployments: some tenants require strict model pinning (no fallback). PRD needs to include tenant-level override and observable flag when fallback is suppressed.
Casey: Ops question — who gets notified on fallback spikes? propose alert to oncall + policy owner when fallback rate > 1% for 5m. Add metric: fallback_rate, fallback_latency_delta, compatibility_score_histogram.
Alex: Good. I'll update PRD with: compat scoring pipeline, TTL + KV invalidation rules, tenant overrides, and the canary/rollback criteria. Will also add the alert rules Casey suggested.
Maya: small UX ask — Console should show per-request which variant served and why (policy decision). tiny snippet: "served_variant": "rw-llama-70b-q4", "decision_reason": "compatibility_pass + region_unavailable"
deploy-bot: Canary started for request-orchestration v0.1 in eu-west-1 :rocket:
Sam: :thumbsup: let's run the compatibility suite against the top 20 customer prompts before next sync.
Priya: I'll add the eval set and the harness to the onboarding pipeline. targeting automations by EOD Wed.
Alex: Thanks all — I'll circulate updated PRD tomorrow and tag folks for final sign-off. if no major blockers, target staged rollout next week.
Casey: noted. if we hit any perf regressions during canary, ops will pause and notify the team.
Maya: LGTM pending the tokenizer rule being explicit.
Alex: Noted — explicit tokenizer rule being added. thanks everyone.
